title: Hickory-Braised Pinto Beans with Molasses Gravy
description: Soft pinto beans sit in a smoky molasses gravy made with hickory broth, mild paprika and a little smooth tomato puree.
equipment: Small enamel Dutch oven with lid

ingredients.name: fully cooked pinto beans
ingredients.note: Choose no-salt-added canned beans or home-cooked beans that mash easily; rinse and drain.

ingredients.name: low-sodium mushroom broth
ingredients.note: Choose plain broth made with mushrooms and water.

steps.title: Preheat the Traeger
steps.text: Preheat the Traeger Silverton 610 to 275°F with hickory pellets and the lid closed, about 15 minutes.

steps.title: Smoke the paprika broth
steps.text: Bring {broth} and {paprika} to a simmer in the Dutch oven on the stove. Set the uncovered pot on the grate for 20 minutes with the Traeger lid closed.

steps.title: Braise the beans
steps.text: Stir {beans} into the broth, fit the pot lid immediately and keep the smoker at 275°F. There is no stall or wrap temperature. Braise for 25–40 minutes, until the bean centers reach 165°F and crush easily.

steps.title: Rest the beans
steps.text: Rest covered for 5 minutes. Ladle most of the hot cooking liquid into the HexClad, leaving a little around the beans.

steps.title: Build the molasses gravy
steps.text: Whisk {molasses}, {sugar}, {tomato}, {mustard} and {vinegar} into the cooking liquid in the HexClad. Bring the smooth base to a simmer.

steps.title: Thicken the sauce
steps.text: Bring the base to a simmer. Whisk in the freshly stirred slurry and let it bubble for 1 minute, stirring until it coats the back of a spoon.

steps.title: Coat and soften
steps.text: Crush about a third of the beans against the side of the pot to break their skins. Fold the soft beans into the gravy in the HexClad and divide them among shallow bowls.

notes: Make ahead: Fully cook the beans ahead if starting from dry. The smoker stage uses already tender beans. Refrigerate the finished beans for up to 3 days. Freezer-Friendly Verdict: Yes. Freeze with enough gravy to cover for up to 2 months. The beans soften further and can be mashed into the sauce. Fridge reheat: Warm a single portion, covered, in the HexClad with a splash of broth or water. Stir or turn gently and heat to 165°F throughout. Freezer reheat: Thaw overnight in the refrigerator. Use the same covered reheating method and heat the center to 165°F. Option A uses smooth tomato and vinegar. For gentler Option B, replace the puree with an equal volume of smooth peeled sweet pepper puree and omit the vinegar. Estimated nutrition per serving (1/4 of recipe): 217 kcal, 12.4 g protein, 40.9 g total carbohydrate, 1.1 g fat, 12.0 g fiber, 14 mg sodium. Includes the measured broth and sauce. Sodium varies with your broth.
